previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old male with a history of non-ischemic cardiomyopathy (LVEF 25%), ICD, chronic kidney disease, and recent heart failure exacerbation was admitted for altered mental status, nausea, and vomiting following increased Percocet use for a right humeral fracture. Evaluation revealed no acute intracranial or abdominal pathology on imaging, and labs showed stable renal function with mild hyperkalemia. Symptoms were attributed to opiate toxicity, exacerbated by reduced kidney clearance. Percocet was discontinued, mental status improved, and pain was transitioned to Vicodin with close monitoring. Lisinopril was restarted, spironolactone held due to hyperkalemia, and heart failure management continued with torsemide. The patient was discharged home with improved cognition, stable labs, and follow-up plans for labs, primary care, and cardiology.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ year old man with past medical history of non-ischemic 
cardiomyopathy (EF 25%), NSVT s/p ICD, s/p AAA repair, PVD, HTN, 
CKD, presents with with SOB.  

ACTIVE PROBLEMS 
1. SOB: Acute on chronic exacerbation of CHF was thought to be 
the cause of patients SOG given signs of left sided failure on 
admission and CXR. Patient responded well to 80mg lasix IV daily 
while being kept on his home dose of 20mg torsemide. By day of 
discharge patient had no crackles on exam and was ambulating 
well around the floor without oxygen requirement. Patient was 
discharged with increased torsemide increased to 60mg po bid. Of 
note, patient continues to smoke and was strongly encouraged to 
quit smoking.

2. DIABETES: Home glipizide was held during hospital stay and 
patient was managed with Humalog ISS. Blood sugars ran 
consistently in the 200's day after admission and patient was 
started on a low dose of lantus 5qhs to supplement humalog ISS. 
Blood glucose improved into the low 100's the following morning, 
and patient was placed back on home glipizide on discharge. He 
was instructed to follow BG levels with PCP.

3. INSOMNIA: Patient reported having difficulty sleeping at 
night both at home and in the hospital leading to napping 
throughout most of the day and compounding his history of 
depression. Psychiatry was consulted and recommended starting 
mirtazipine 15mg qhs to help patient sleep, with possibility of 
titrating off imipramine to miratzipine in the future.

4. DEPRESSION: Patient admitted to depressed mood with anhedonia 
and insomnia during his stay, but denied any psychoses, SI or 
HI. He has a history of depression, and patient was continued on 
his outpatient regiment of perphenazine and imipramine, which he 
has been on for many years. Psychiatry was consulted as per 
above,  and recommended continuing his home treatment. Patient 
was strongly encouraged to follow up with his outpatient 
psychiatrist, although an appointment could not be made prior to 
discharge.

CHRONIC PROBLEMS
1. Hx of symptomatic NSVT with 1st degree AVB. Patient was 
continued on home does of amiodarone and was asymptomatic during 
his stay. Of note, patient believes his SOB may have worsened 
since starting amiodarone. Will defer this possibility to 
primary cardiologist.

2. Nonischemic cardiomyopathy with LV thrombus. Patient has poor 
systolic function (LVEF 25%) and was noted to have LV thrombus 
earlier this year. INR was 1.9 at admission, and patient was 
maintained on home dosing of coumadin. INR decreased to 1.5 on 
day of discharge, and coumadin was increased to 4mg daily. 
Patient was given lab slip and instructed to follow up INR

3. Arm fracture: Patient continued to complain of right arm pain 
following fall earlier this year. Xray demonstrated persistent 
fracture of the surgical neck of
the right proximal humerus and greater tuberosity fracture. Pain 
was treated with tylenol prn and was instructed to follow up 
with orthopedics and pain managment clinics where he is already 
established.

3. GERD: Patient was maintained on his home dose of omeprazole

TRANSITIONAL ISSUES.
-INR was found to be subtherapeutic, and his coumadin has been 
increased to 4mg daily. Patient was given lab slip to check INR 
in two days and to fax results to his PCP for management. 
-Blood glucose was running high (200's in the afternoon) on his 
home glipizide, and increased monitoring may be warranted.

Discharge Instructions:
Dear Mr. ___,

You were admitted to the hospital because you were having 
shortness of breath. This was due to retaining fluid because of 
your congestive heart failure. We treated this by using 
medication to remove extra fluid from your body. Additionally, 
we think that your chronic shortness of breath might be due to 
your COPD and smoking. It's very important to stop smoking and 
follow up with your primary care doctor to address these lung 
issues. We also had psychiatry see your because you have been 
feeling depressed recently and having trouble sleeping. They 
recommended you start taking a medication called Remeron at 
night to help you sleep. Finally, we found that your blood 
wasn't thinned enough, and we would like you to increase your 
dose of coumadin as outlined below. It has been a pleasure 
taking care of you.

Please weigh yourself every morning, and call your doctor if 
weight goes up more than 3 lbs. Also, please attend the 
appoinments with your doctors we have made below and try to set 
up an appointment to see your psychiatrist within a month to 
address your sleeping problems and depression.

CHANGES TO YOUR MEDICATIONS
START Remeron 15mg every night before bedtime.
STOP Niacin
INCREASE torsemide from 20mg twice a day to 60mg once a day.
INCREASE coumadin to 4mg every day.
DECREASE simvastatin to 10mg daily
PLEASE use lab slip to check INR in two days and have results 
faxed to your PCP.
